limited_overlap.description: applicants with education between 17 and 18: 53% of the 1345 training applicants there have an enrolment propensity outside the overlap bounds, so the effect for them rests on the outcome model rather than on comparable enrolled and non-enrolled applicants.

applicants with prior_earnings between 41,370 and 928,180: 91% of the 3000 training applicants there have an enrolment propensity outside the overlap bounds, so the effect for them rests on the outcome model rather than on comparable enrolled and non-enrolled applicants.

applicants with months_unemployed equal to 0: 54% of the 1463 training applicants there have an enrolment propensity outside the overlap bounds, so the effect for them rests on the outcome model rather than on comparable enrolled and non-enrolled applicants.
applicants whose follow-up earnings are not recorded: their effect is identified only if non-response is unrelated to earnings given the adjustment set and enrolment (1972 training applicants).

warnings: Enrolled and non-enrolled applicants differ in pre-enrolment columns: mean prior earnings 17,957 against 37,900; the estimates adjust for the columns listed under roles.
experience is an exact linear combination of the other pre-enrolment columns; it is not put in the adjustment set, and its information is carried by the columns it is built from.

No covariate passed the claim rule (joint p below 0.05 in the primary fit, at the median of four nuisance fits, with one sign). Candidates by median joint p: prior_earnings p=0.0402 (+761, +2465, +981, +1051 dollars per SD); region p=0.0739 (-3416, -2925, -2856, -2941 dollars per SD); parttime p=0.122 (-1297, -20, -1541, -1168 dollars per SD); smsa p=0.125 (+1152, +1492, +1334, +1290 dollars per SD). The joint p-value of each covariate moved across fold splits (the single-split fit gave p near 0.004 for age and 0.03 for prior earnings), so no covariate is claimed as an effect modifier.
23.5% of training rows have a cross-fitted propensity outside the overlap bounds; the all-rows ATE depends on the outcome model in those rows, and the overlap-bounded estimate is 3,699 dollars.
Instrument check (age, responders only): complier effect 50,972 dollars with 90% interval [-15,277, 117,221], against the ATE 5,968. The complier effect and the ATE are different quantities.
Certificate and hours worked are measured during or after the program and are mediators; they are not adjusted for, so the estimates are total effects that include the paths through them.

Test applicants differ from training applicants in means: prior_earnings 31,737.8 (train) against 25,788.0 (test); months_unemployed 2.7 (train) against 3.2 (test). Per-applicant effects for test applicants outside the training range are extrapolated.

Test applicants outside the propensity overlap bounds: 6.4%. 256 of the 800 applicants at the top of the cate order are among them; their effects come from the outcome model, not from comparable enrolled and non-enrolled applicants. Restricting the top group to the overlap region gives 800 applicants with mean cate 6,653 dollars.
Test applicants outside the training range of an effect-model term: 2.5%.

No covariate passed the modifier rule, so no effect modifier is claimed. The per-applicant effects and the ranking come from a model on the lead covariates ['prior_earnings', 'region', 'parttime'], whose evidence is weak; the ranking carries less information than the interval widths suggest.
